header.title: KV 17: Grab Sethos' I.〈, vordere rechte Seitenkammer der Sargkammer〉: AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Literary texts
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:egy:tla:sawlit:kv-17-grab-sethos-i-vordere-rechte-seitenkammer-der-sargkamm:translit, from the Thesaurus Linguae Aegyptiae (2018), in Simon Schweitzer's AED-TEI (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.
header.availability: CC BY-SA 4.0, as its source requires: credit the Thesaurus Linguae Aegyptiae (2018), in Simon Schweitzer's AED-TEI and this AI translation, and share adaptations under the same licence.

notes.1.1: Line 3: 'md,t r ḫft,j.pl Rꜥ' is unclear. Line 9: ḫt,jw may be 'following' or 'terraces'. Lines 12-13: jmi̯ is read as the negative verb ('do not let'); as the imperative of rḏi̯ it would mean 'let'. Line 14 is uncertain. Line 32: ḥ{ꜣ}[m]w is a doubtful reading. Line 42: or 'by diminishing them'. Line 43: šbb.t, the beer mash of line 53; its use here is unclear. Line 49: ddj.t, a red mineral (ochre or haematite) from Elephantine. Line 51: ḥnsk.ttj, 'the one with the braid', a title at Heliopolis. Line 56: 'days of going upstream' obscure. Line 62: sḏr.t, a drink that brings sleep. Line 72 plays on jmꜣ.yt 'gracious' and Imau. Lines 73-74: jp ḥm.t ('counting maidservants') obscure. Lines 76-77 obscure. Line 80: sp-n-jwtj uncertain. Line 85: doubtful reading. Line 87 obscure. Line 92 damaged. Lines 106-107 uncertain. Line 111 obscure and possibly corrupt. Lines 122-127 play on ḥtp/Field of Peace (the Field of Offerings), jꜣ/Field of Reeds, jḫ.t 'things'/jḫjḫ 'glitterers'. Line 130 plays on ḥḥ 'millions' and the Heh-gods. Lines 136-137 ambiguous (zꜣ may also be 'protection'). Lines 138-173 are directions and captions for the painted cow; many captions (149-172) are obscure, and 173's names are unidentified. Line 185: ḥꜥb uncertain. Line 192 obscure. Line 193: smꜥ~hj taken as 'make forget'. Line 199: Jw-n-bꜣ.wj unidentified. Line 201: sjd and the syntax are unclear. Lines 204-211 pun on hꜣb/ibis, ḫn/tḫn.j (an unidentified creature), jnḥ/moon, ꜥnꜥn/baboon. Line 213: wbꜣ unclear. Lines 217-218: two different words for natron (ḥsmn, bd). Lines 226, 229, 231 uncertain. Lines 236 and 238 obscure; Ḥwj.t taken as Rain. Line 242: Bakhu, the mountain of sunrise. Line 251: skk uncertain. Line 255: rd.w štꜣ.w unclear. Line 265: ꜥꜣ read as 'here'. jp{n}[.w]=st r ḥm,t.pl may instead mean 'its quantity is to be reckoned according to the maidservants'. mḥ šzp=s 4 m rꜥ~y[,t] may instead be an instruction, 'fill in her four hooves with pigment'.

nodes.text: [Now] [it came to pass] [that] [Ra] [rose], the god who came into being by himself, after he had been in kingship,
mankind and the gods being [one] thing.
Then mankind [were] [plotting] [words] [...] words, as(?) enemies of Ra.
[Now] His Majesty, may he live, prosper and be healthy, had grown old:
his bones were silver,
his flesh gold,
his hair [true] lapis lazuli.
Then [His] [Majesty] [perceived] [the words] [that] [were plotted] against him by mankind.
Then His Majesty, may he live, prosper and be healthy, said to those who were in his following:
Summon to me my Eye, and Shu, Tefnut, Geb and Nut, with the fathers and mothers who were with me when I was in Nun, and the god Nun as well;
let him bring his courtiers with him. You shall bring them in secret:
do not let mankind see,
do not let their hearts take flight. You shall come with them to the Great Mansion,
that they may give their firm(?) counsel, [since] I came from Nun to the place where I came into being.
Then these gods were brought [at once],
and these gods [stood] on his two sides, touching the ground with their foreheads before His Majesty,
so that he might speak his words before the eldest father, the maker of mankind, king of the *rekhyt* [common people].
Then they said before His Majesty:
Speak to us, that we may hear it.
Then Ra said to Nun:
Eldest god, in whom I came into being, ancestor gods: look, mankind, who came into being from my Eye, have plotted against me.
Tell me what you would do about it,
for see, I am searching [for counsel];
I will not kill them until I have heard what you will say about it.
Then the Majesty of Nun said:
My son Ra, god greater than the one who made him, mightier than those who created him, remain on [your] throne!
Great is the fear of you; your Eye shall be against those who plot against you.
Then the Majesty of Ra said:
Look, they have fled into the desert,
their hearts afraid because of what [I] [said] [to] them.
Then they said before His Majesty:
Let your Eye go, that it may smite(?) for you those who plotted evil.
There is no eye more preeminent than it [for] [smiting] [them] [for] [you].
Let it go down as Hathor.
Then this goddess came back, having slain mankind in the desert.
Then the Majesty of this god said:
Welcome in peace, Hathor, who has done for the Maker(?) [that] [for which] [I] [came]!
Then this goddess said:
As you live for me, I have prevailed over mankind, and it was sweet to my heart.
Then the Majesty of Ra said:
I shall have power over them [as] [king].
Do not diminish them!
That is how Sekhmet came into being, the mash(?) of the night, to wade in their blood from Herakleopolis onward.
Then [Ra] said:
Summon to me swift messengers who hurry, that they may run [like] the shadow of a body.
Then these messengers were brought at once.
Then the Majesty of this god said:
Hurry to Elephantine,
bring me *didi* [a red substance] in great quantity.
Then this *didi* was brought to him.
Then [the Majesty] [of] [this] [great] [god] had the [Braided One] who is in Heliopolis grind this *didi*,
while maidservants were crushing barley for beer.
Then this *didi* was put into this mash,
[and it was] [like] the [blood] of men.
Then 7,000 jars of beer were made.
Then the Majesty of the Dual King Ra came with these gods to see this beer, now that the land had dawned for the slaughter of mankind by the goddess on their days of going upstream(?).
Words spoken by the Majesty of Ra:
How good it is!
I shall protect mankind with it.
Then Ra said:
Carry it, then, to the place where she said: I shall slay mankind there.
Then the Majesty of the Dual King Ra rose early, in the depth of the night, to have this sleeping-draught poured out.
Then the fields were filled three palms [deep] with the liquid, by the might of the Majesty of this god.
Then this goddess went out in the morning
and found these [fields] flooded.
Then her face was pleased there.
Then she drank, and it was good to her heart.
She came back drunk,
without having recognised mankind.
Then the Majesty of Ra said to this goddess:
Welcome in peace, gracious one!
That is how the beautiful women of Imau came into being.
Then the Majesty of Ra said to this goddess: Sleeping-draughts shall be made for her at the seasons [of] the year, assigned(?) to her by the maidservants.
That is how the making of sleeping-draughts at [the counting of her maidservants](?), the festival of Hathor, by all people came into being, since the first day.
Then the Majesty of Ra said to this goddess:
Has the burning of pain caused pain(?)?
That is how the duty(?) of respect(?) came into being, through the sufferer(?).
Then the Majesty of Ra said:
As I live for myself, my heart is very weary of being with them.
I slew them, a matter of nothing(?);
there is no shortness in the reach of my arm.
What the gods who were in his following said: Do not flee(?) in your weariness; you have power over what you wish.
Then the Majesty of this god said to the Majesty of Nun:
My limbs are feeble for the first time;
I will not wait(?) until another overtakes me.
Then the Majesty of Nun said:
Son Shu, [let] [your] eye [be] for [your] father, as his protection(?);
daughter Nut, put him [on] [your] [back]!
Then Nut said:
How so, my father Nun?
So said Nut.
Nut became [a] [cow],
and then the Majesty of Ra [...] on her back.
Then these people [came] [from the place where they had fled to(?)],
and they saw him on the back of the cow.
[Then] these people said to him:
[Rebellion has been made] [against] [you](?).
[Come](?) to us, that we may overthrow your enemies who plotted against the one who made them.
His Majesty proceeded to [his] palace [...] of this cow,
[and he did not(?)] [go(?)] with them.
Then the land was in darkness.
When the land grew bright in the morning(?), these people came out with bows and sticks [...],
[and] they [raised(?)] an arm to shoot at the enemies.
Then the Majesty of this god said:
Your misdeeds(?) are behind you, you slaughterers!
Slaughter is far [from(?)] [the beginning(?)].
That is how slaughter came into being among [mankind].
Then this god said to Nut:
[I] have put myself on [your] back to raise myself up.
What is this? Nut says(?), having come into being there as(?) the [two] skies(?).
[Said] the Majesty of this god:
Keep yourself far from them!
Raise me up!
Look at me!
That is how she became [the] [sky].
Then the Majesty of [this] god was looking out from within her.
She said:
If only you would furnish [it] for me with multitudes!
That is how [...] came into being.
[Then] His [Majesty], may he live, prosper and be healthy, [said]:
A field is at peace here!
That is how the Field of Peace came into being.
Ah, I will grow plants in it!
That is how the Field of [Reeds] came into being.
[I] will furnish it with all things.
[That is how] the glittering ones, the stars, came into being.
Then Nut began to tremble because of [the height].
[Then] the Majesty [of] Ra [said]:
If only I had millions to hold her up!
That is how the Heh-gods came into being.
Then the Majesty of Ra said:
My son Shu, place yourself under [my] daughter Nut;
guard for me the Heh-gods, the Heh-gods there, who live in the twilight;
put her on your head and nurse her.
That is how the giving of a son as nurse(?) to a daughter came into being.
That is how a father's placing of a son on his head came into being.
This spell is to be spoken over a cow, with Heh-gods who are at her breast and Heh-gods who are at her back.
One cubit, her palms 4(?), in paint(?).
Nine stars on her belly,
it(?) emerging(?) from the hindquarters, which are in front of her two legs.
Shu under her belly,
made in yellow,
his two arms under these stars,
made with his name between them, namely: Shu himself.
A bark with a steering-oar(?) and a shrine in it, the sun-disk above it, Ra in it, in front of Shu, beside his hand;
another version: behind him, beside his hand.
Her two udders made in the middle of her two left legs.
Their side made with writing in the middle of the leg, reading: Outside(?).
I am there(?).
I will not let [it] be done,
them going down(?).
[That] which is under the bark that is in front, reading:
You shall not grow weary, my son!
Them going down(?).
Reading:
Your condition is like living [forever].
Reading: There(?)
your protection is in me.
Life, prosperity and health to this nose of yours!
[That] which is behind Shu, beside his arm, reading:
Guard them!
[That] which is behind him at his side, going down(?), reading:
[Truly(?)] they enter, while [I] withdraw(?) every day.
[That] which is under the arm of the figure that is under the left leg, behind it, reading:
Sealing all things.
[That] which is on his head, under the hindquarters of the cow, which is at her legs, reading:
The one belonging to his going forth(?).
[That] which is behind the two figures that are at her two legs, on their heads:
Praise [in] the necropolis(?).
Office is given, too, when he enters.
[That] which is on the head of the two figures that are between her two thighs:
[Dua]mut[ef], Idem(?), Was-herut(?).
Then the Majesty of this god said to Thoth:
Summon for me the Majesty of Geb, saying:
Come,
hurry at once!
Then the Majesty of Geb came.
Then the Majesty of this god said:
Do battle against(?) your serpents that are in you!
Look, they were afraid of me while I was [there].
And you yourself know their magic powers.
Go now to the place where my father Nun [is],
and tell him: Guard the creatures of land and water! And also make writings of yours for every mound of your serpents that are there, saying:
Beware of disturbing(?) anything!
Let them know [that] I am here.
Look, I shine forth [...] I am there for them.
Look too: as for their founding(?), it is he who will be in this land forever.
And beware of those magicians who know their spells.
Look, magic itself is there.
Look, whoever swallows it, look, [it is I].
Never has it happened that I was hindered(?) by a great one who came into being before me.
I will commit them to your son Osiris, to guard their young and make the hearts of their elders forget(?) there
their magic powers, which they work as they please against the whole land, with their spells that are in their bellies.
Then the Majesty of this god said:
Summon Thoth to me!
Then he was brought at once.
Then the Majesty of this god said to Thoth:
Look, [I] am here in the sky, in my place, since [I] am to make light [and] radiance(?) in the Duat and the Island of the Two Bas(?).
You shall write there,
and you shall bring low(?) those who are among them, those whom we made, who made rebellion among the Akeru [earth gods], the followers of this angry-hearted one.
You shall be in my place [as] deputy,
and so you shall be called Thoth, deputy of Ra.
[I] will also let you send out those greater than you.
That is how the ibis of Thoth came into being.
I will also let you stretch out your hand before the face of the primeval gods who are greater than you, and good is my word(?) that you carry out.
That is how the *tekheni* of Thoth came into being.
I will also let you encircle the two skies with your beauty and with your brightness.
That is how the moon of Thoth came into being.
I will also let you turn back(?) the Haunebut.
That is how the baboon(?) of Thoth came into being.
That is how [he] came to be vizier. You shall also be my deputy,
with all who see you being opened(?) through you,
and everything [I] have made praising god for you.
A man shall say this spell over himself, anointed with moringa oil and unguent,
[a censer] in his two hands with incense,
natron behind his two ears,
natron on his mouth,
his clothing [being] two new garments,
having purified himself in floodwater, shod in two white sandals,
with a Maat(?) drawn on his tongue in [green] scribal paint.
If Thoth's heart is set on reciting it for Ra, he purifies himself with a purification of 9 days.
Servants [among] people shall do likewise.
As for the one who recites it, [if] he performs this rite that is in this book, he will spend his lifetime in the midst of [...] more(?).
His two eyes shall be his, all his limbs shall be his,
his steps shall not go astray(?),
and it shall be said of him by people: He is like Ra on the day he was born.
His goods shall not grow less,
his gate shall not be defiled(?).
Truly correct, a million times.
Nun was embraced(?) by the Great One himself.
He said to the gods who come forth in the east [of] the sky:
Give praise to the eldest god, from whom I came into being!
I am the one who made the sky and set [it] firm [to] [place] [the bas] [of the gods] [in] [it], and I am with them [for] the eternity that the years have borne.
[Magic] is my *ba* [manifestation].
It is greater than that(?).
The *ba* of Shu is Khnum.
The *ba* of [eternity] is Rain(?).
The *ba* of darkness is Night.
The *ba* of Nun is Ra.
The *ba* of Osiris is the Ram of Mendes.
The *ba*s of Sobek are the crocodiles; the *ba* of every god is in the snakes; the *ba* of Apophis is in Bakhu; the *ba* of Ra is throughout the whole land.
A man says, when he makes his protection by magic:
I am that pure magic which is in the mouth and the body [of] Ra.
Gods, keep far from me!
I am Ra, radiance(?).
You shall say [it] when you pass by in the evening and in the morning.
On your face!
Fall, enemy of Ra!
I am his *ba*, magic.

O Lord of [eternity], creator of everlastingness, who wipes out(?) the years of the gods, into whom Ra descends, lord of his god, ruler of the one who made him, you whom the fathers of the gods love, pure magic upon his head! Make a female figure standing on your southern [side](?),
make a goddess upon it, in its middle a snake standing on its tail,
her hand on its belly,
its tail on the ground.

He to whom Thoth gives office, the dignity of the sky upon him, to whom Shu gives [his] two arms against(?) him: I am rescued from these two great gods who sit in the east [of] the sky, guardians of the sky, guardians of the earth, who make the hidden ones grow(?).
Then they say:
How great he is when he goes forth to see Nun!
Words to be spoken [by] one who is pure in(?) the month, on [...] 1[5]th(?) [day], [like] this former rite.
He who says this spell shall live in the necropolis;
great shall be the fear of him among those on earth.
If they say: Who? — your names are [Eternity] and Everlastingness.
Then they say:
[He is] [a god] [in] [truth].
Then they say:
He has arrived here(?) on the road.
